newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parliament to elect president Monday.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parliament to elect president Monday.

text.p: Albania's parliament, made up mainly of the ruling Democratic Party, said on Thursday it would hold a vote to elect a president next Monday.

President Sali Berisha, who had to seek re-election by March 9, was chosen earlier by the Democrats as their candidate and he was sure to be given a fresh five-year mandate as his party holds 122 of 140 parliamentary seats.
"On Monday at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), a plenary session of parliament will be convened to elect the president of the republic," said parliamentary president Pjeter Arbnori.
Berisha was likely to face the election unopposed as smaller rightist opposition parties declined to put up a challenger.

The main opposition Socialist Party has boycotted parliament after last year's disputed general election. Socialist leader Fatos Nano, Berisha's key political rival, is in jail for corruption, though his supporters allege he is being held as a political prisoner.
The setting of the election date was announced after a four-hour debate on three weeks of protests over a pyramid scheme scandal in the southern town of Vlore.
